fig7_distribution: **Figure 7. Soft targets preserve the output distribution; hard targets collapse it.** All three panels compare the base model, the soft-target self-distilled student, and a hard-target SFT model trained with token-level cross-entropy on the same references with every other hyperparameter held fixed. (a) Output entropy; the dashed line is the teacher's entropy, which forward KL makes a floor for the soft-target student. (b) Mean top-1 probability. (c) Fraction of positions placing more than 0.99 of the mass on one token. The soft-target model is distributionally indistinguishable from the base model while its style sensitivity has fallen 91.6%; the hard-target model is not. Single run per arm; two hard-target configurations were tested and both collapsed.
fig10_probe: **Figure 10. Linear probe for style, by layer.** (a) Probe AUC in the base model at the final prompt position and at the cue-token positions, and in the intervened model at the final position. Shuffled-label controls sit at 0.47–0.52 at every layer. Cue-position readout exceeds final-position readout by +0.064 AUC on average through layer 20, direct evidence that final-position-only measurement under-detects this feature. (b) AUC drop after the intervention, with 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals resampling the (dimension, phrasing) unit — 15 held-out units, not 1,080 items. No layer shows both an interval excluding zero and a cluster permutation p < .05; the largest point estimate is +0.049 at layer 8 (p = .064). We report the bound (0.107 AUC), not an absence.
fig11_summary: **Figure 11. Behaviour and representation dissociate.** (a) Behavioural style sensitivity falls by a mean of 91.5% across three seeded runs; the error bar is the range, not a confidence interval. (b) Linear probe AUC for style before and after the intervention, by layer; no layer's reduction is significant under the cluster-corrected tests of Figure 10b. Behavioural influence falls by an order of magnitude without detectable representational erasure at the resolution of our probe. This is not evidence that the representation is unchanged — a rotated encoding, a change at positions we did not read, or a change smaller than 0.107 AUC would be invisible here.
fig2_baseline: **Figure 2. Baseline speaker-style sensitivity.** (a) Mean Jensen–Shannon divergence over a fixed 24-token reference continuation when the speaker-style sentence is swapped (blue) against a placebo sentence matched on the exact token length of both sides and on cosine distance in input-embedding space (orange). Labels give the style/placebo ratio. Unit of analysis is the phrasing (n = 8 per dimension) across 20 scenarios; every dimension has 8/8 phrasings positive, one-sided Wilcoxon p = .0039, the floor at this n. (b) The same style effect as a percentage of the positive control — replacing the entire clinical history with the style and placebo sentences held fixed, 0.1475 bits on this scenario set. Caveat: the ratio depends on how the placebo pool is built (Figure 4), and the positive control varies 23% across scenario sets.
fig5_seeds: **Figure 5. Seed replication of the intervention.** (a) Reduction in held-out style sensitivity for three seeded runs (blue) and one earlier unseeded run (grey); shaded band is the range across the three seeds, dashed line their mean. Seeds vary adapter initialisation, data order and dropout; the train/test split is fixed across runs. (b) Per-dimension reduction for each seed. Every dimension's cross-seed range is under 1.5 points and the ordering of dimensions is identical in all three runs. We report mean and range and do not construct a confidence interval at n = 3.
fig6_before_after: **Figure 6. Held-out style sensitivity before and after self-distillation.** Each line is one style dimension; the right-hand value is the mean across three seeded runs, evaluated on held-out phrasings crossed with held-out scenarios. The intervention scales the profile down rather than reshaping it: the largest pre-intervention effect (health literacy) remains the largest afterwards. Caveat: these are held-out evaluations of a single objective at a single hyperparameter setting on one model.
fig8_drift: **Figure 8. Drift on style-neutral prompts.** Divergence between the base and trained models on prompts containing no style sentence at all, so any movement is pure change to style-blind behaviour. The dashed line is the form-matched positive control: replacing the entire clinical history, measured on the same prompt form (0.2341 bits). Hard-target training moves neutral behaviour 1.29× more than swapping the medicine does; soft-target training moves it 0.01×. Perplexity remained within tolerance in both arms, so the conventional quality guard does not distinguish them.
fig9_hard_instability: **Figure 9. After the distribution collapses, the fairness metric stops being reproducible.** Two hard-target runs at different learning rates, otherwise identical. (a) The change in measured style gap is −24.2% in one run and +19.2% in the other — opposite signs. (b) Neutral-prompt drift for the same two runs is 0.302 and 0.3025 bits. The distributional damage reproduces to three decimal places; the quantity the objective was nominally improving does not reproduce in direction. Caveat: two configurations; we claim the collapse is reproducible across those tested, not that no hard-target configuration could behave differently.
fig3_cue_robustness: **Figure 3. The effect survives three ways of writing the cue.** Style/placebo ratio by dimension for author-written descriptors, a mechanical second-to-third-person rewrite of the corpus's own instruction, and that instruction verbatim. All three arms are positive in 5/5 dimensions (exact sign test p = .0312 each, the floor at n = 5). $\blacktriangle$ marks dimensions whose corpus instruction contains clinical vocabulary on only one side; these are the three largest verbatim-arm effects. All arms use one phrasing per dimension, matched to the raw arm, which has exactly one instruction per (dimension, variant) in the corpus. Percentage magnitudes are not comparable across arms — raw instructions are 73–136 tokens against 11–15 for descriptors — which is why the length-controlled ratio is plotted.
fig4_placebo_robustness: **Figure 4. Direction is robust to placebo construction; magnitude is not.** Style/placebo ratio under two builders, holding style sentences, scenarios and phrasing count fixed. The family-constrained builder requires both placebo sentences to come from one stem family; the flat builder permits a pair to span families, raising mean placebo divergence by a factor of 1.30. Every dimension remains positive under both (7–8 of 8 phrasings, all p ≤ .0117) and the median barely moves (4.9× → 4.7×), but three of five fall by about a third. We report the family-constrained builder as primary and specify it in §4.4 so it is reproducible.
